## Write scale_fill_semantic()

So we'll use deeptime::scale_fill_geopattern as a basis, but instead of `deeptime:::geo_pattern(code)` we'll use `llm_vec_classify(code, bigpal)`... where code is the variable to encode...

```{r}
bigpal <- c("blue", "grey", "aquamarine", "turquoise", "darkgrey") 

library(mall)
options(.mall_chat = ellmer::chat_google_gemini())


rep("dolphin", 15) |> mall::llm_vec_classify(labels = bigpal)

```

<details>


```{r}
vec_to_vec <- function(x, to = NULL){ifelse(x == "cat", "black", "white")}

vec_to_self <- function(x, to  = NULL){x}



translator <- function(mapped_var, to = NULL, table = NULL, how = vec_to_self) {
      if (is.na(mapped_var)) {
        na_value
      } else {
        if(is.null(table)){
          mapped_var |> how(to)
        } else {
            # lookup routine
          }
        
        
        # deeptime:::geo_pattern(code)   #<<< this is the only change
      }
    }

#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggproto ScaleDiscrete
#' @keywords internal
ScaleDiscreteTranslate <- ggproto("ScaleDiscreteTranslate", ScaleDiscrete,
  map = function(self, x, limits = self$get_limits()) {
    na_value <- if (self$na.translate) self$na.value else NA
    # clean limits
    limits <- limits[!is.na(limits)]
    # if no limits, just return a bunch of NA values
    if (length(limits) < 1) {
      return(rep(list(na_value), length(x)))
    }

    # convert to character
    if (is.factor(x)) {
      x <- as.character(x)
    }

    # filter to limits
    x[is.na(match(x, limits))] <- NA

    # get patterns
    sapply(x, translator, simplify = FALSE)
  }
)
```

</details>

```{r}
tribble(~animal, ~count,~color, 
        "cat",        1, "red",
        "peacock",    2, "green",
        "piglet",     3, "blue") |> 
ggplot() + 
  aes(fill = color,
      x = animal,
      y = count) + 
  geom_col() + 
  scale_fill_translate()

layer_data()

tribble(~animal, ~count, ~color, 
        "cat",        10, "red",
        "peacock",    20, "green",
        "piglet",    30, "blue") |> 
  uncount(count) |>
  ggplot() + 
  aes(fill = color,
      x = animal) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  scale_fill_translate()

layer_data()
```


Hearing about @willgearty's scale_fill_geopattern 🙌🚀🤩🙏🙏, I wondered if this is in neighboring space. I guess all scales for me look a little bit alike, because I haven't done a ton of scale specification (I'm not color confident, which seems like a prerequisite for a lot of extension scale work).

Anyway, it seems like there's a lookup table that scale_fill_geopattern uses which helps translate from numeric id (maybe name too) to pattern, and scale_geometry() translates from id to to boundaries (or other geometry like coordinates, paths)... Could we say that scale_fill_geopattern is a semantic encoder? (Can we say that of scale_geometry?)

And the more non-deterministic translations discussed in #151 translators from category -> color, assisted by LLMs (maybe MALL) would have a slightly different configuration, where you'd have a vector of items (menu) from which to select from instead of a lookup table.

I guess I think a scale_translate_deteministic(aesthetics = "fill, lookup_table = id_geopattern_df, etc, etc  )... would deliver the appropriate translation (as scale_fill_geopattern already does).

And scale_translate_stochastic(aesthetics = "color" , to_menu =  c("olivedrab", "bisque", "saddlebrown", "plum3"), translation_method = mall::llm_vec_classify,  etc, etc   )... would 🤞 translate aes(color = c("frog", "horse")) to rendered "olivedrab" and "saddlebrown"

Maybe these scales sit between scale_identity and scale_discrete, cause that their identity is informative, and the 'vanilla' discrete scale ignores pretty much strips away identity?
